To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PAMELA limits on the anti-proton spectrum can be used to constrain the neutralino-charging mass difference in the Supersymmetric scenario with light gauginos and heavy sfermions.
the PAMELA anti-proton data can be used to constrain the mass splitting between the neutralino and the charged partners, thus complementing the FERMI results.

we show that the PAMELA antiproton data can be used to put constraints on the neutralino chargino mass splitting, and that the limit obtained in this way is consistent with the one obtained from the FERMI LAT γ-ray data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel use of the anti-protons to constrain models of Dark Matter.
the use of the anti-protons to set a constraint of the neutralino-chargonio mass difference.
a new way of constraining the neutralino mass spectrum by exploiting the PAMELA results.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neutralino-chargino mass degeneracy can be ruled out for neutralino masses below 450 GeV, if it is a pure wino and constitutes all the DM.
the combined PAMELA and γ-ray data can be used to constrain a large region of parameter space for a mixed neutralinos and for a mixed neutralinowino.
the PAMELA data are not able to exclude the wino neutralino scenario for masses above 450 GeV, while the FERMI gamma-ray data can rule it out up to a neutralino mass of 1 TeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PAMELA data can be used to test the neutralino-charging mass degeneracy, while the FERMI data can be used for the thermal Dark Matter cross section.
the PAMELA anti-proton data is competitive with the FERMI γ-ray data in constraining scenarios with large neutralino-charginino mass differences.

PAMELA has set the first constraint on the neutralinos-charginos mass difference, which is complementary to the FERMI limit on the mass degeneracy, and that the combined limits from PAMELA and from FERMI are the most stringent limits to date.
The main takeaway from our work is that
indirect detection experiments can set constraints on the neutralino mass spectrum, thus opening the door to a new era of Dark Matter phenomenology.
the anti-proton data can be exploited to set limits on the mass difference between the LSP and the next to LSP (NLSP).
the PAMELA data can be used as an important complement to the γ-ray data in constraining the Dark Matter phenomenology, especially in the case of the pure wino scenario.
